notes.title: Network Update
notes.content:
We've reduced the amount of bandwidth required for multiplayer by only syncing the pick up and throw events.

This means that you can have more players in a game (4) but it also means differences in physics simulation will mean objects aren't guaranteed to be in the same position on all clients. In practice you probably wont notice.

You should also only use join host on a local network. Otherwise use the quick match option.

notes.title: NAT punch-through beta
notes.content:
Hi,

We need some testers for the new NAT punch-through method.

This method consists of 3 components:
[*]Automatic port forwarding
[*]NAT punch-through facilitator
[*]Direct connection

This will allow 90%~ of users to play online (unless your network or router blocks the above methods e.g. school networks)

If you haven't already port forwarded please try connecting to another player online either with quick match or friends invite (invite accept appears over your controller)

I'm particularly interested in if you are able to connect to the facilitator which will be noted in the output log in the Arcade_Data folder.

Please also note any loss of performance.

To test the new NAT punch-through you have to opt-in to the beta in steam.

Happy testing ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: Release candidate!
notes.content:
The release candidate is available on the beta channel!
This version includes another new game called Honey Rush
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/22269100/3a7eae606edfa6697d15ac0f4264cc9b88e0c142.jpg[/img]
As you can see it's the first joystick game in the arcade. You use the joysticks to control either side of a long pole and you have to guide a ball up a maze of holes to get to the goal. The faster you do it the more points you get.

We need people to test the release candidate ahead of the official release on the 22nd. 

We'll be at EGX on the launch day so expect some delay if you post any messages to us then. Here's what kind of swag you'll be able to grab if you're attending: http://steamcommunity.com/app/435490/discussions/0/343786746000715748/

Here's a little teaser video if you can't wait to see the new machine:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BJlFxzwKQ-g&feature=youtu.be

Future plans were posted here if you missed it:
http://steamcommunity.com/games/435490/announcements/detail/568966177036913287

"Why is X game missing?" - Don't worry, we'll be adding more content post release but we've completed all the goals in Early Access and even exceeded the target number of games as well. If you bought the game today it would feel like a complete experience.

Other changes:
[*]Fixed Rapid Fire hole state bug
[*]Tweaked claw physics
[*]Basketball physics tweak
[*]New music
[*]Graphics slider UI tweaks

EDIT:
Thanks for the feedback, made some more changes:
[*]Adjusted the restricted zones of some machines

notes.title: What next for Pierhead Arcade?
notes.content:
TLDR: Pierhead Arcade will leave Early Access on 22nd September. More content and platforms will be added post release.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/22269100/fd9e0443acb5e1e2b9899e8d64b837076337e516.png[/img]

It's been a fun ride thus far.

I spent a lot of my youth (and some of my adult life) inside arcades and I've had VR on the back of my mind ever since trying a Virtuality style machine for the first time in an arcade as a child. I can't even remember the name of that game but it was standing VR and you had a motion tracked controller which you could use to aim down sites of a low poly gun (it wasn't Dactyle Nightmare). I was blown away by this and even then I knew that hand tracking was key to the experience.

Fast forward to the second coming of VR. I saw what Palmer Luckey was doing with his Rift and I knew that this time VR would stick so I went and backed his kickstarter. A short time later I had the DK1 in my lap and I was making awesome games with it. I knew then that this was the direction I wanted to go in so I left my job and started Mechabit.

Then at EGX I listened to an insightful talk by Chet Faliszek about developing for VR. I approached him afterwards and he liked what we were doing, a few months later I had an early Vive devkit in my office. 

The Vive was so simple and intuitive to use and develop for that we had a simple white box room you could throw balls in minutes after setting it up. It was just so much fun messing around in this room that we kept adding more and more white boxed tables and games to it and thus Pierhead Arcade was born.

We took it to GDC and everyone was blown away by it so we knew we were onto something. The game was still pretty early at that time but we wanted to share it with everyone as soon as possible so we went with Early Access. 

We kept hammering away at it and it's come a long way since then. We feel like the game is really strong now and represents all the things we set out to do when we started. 

I feel like we've come full circle so it's appropriate that we launch the game at EGX this month on the 22nd September. We'll continue to add new content to the game up to and post release but we're confident now that if you bought Pierhead Arcade it would feel like a complete game. 

After that we'll be porting the game to other VR platforms so that more people get to enjoy the experience of running around in their own arcade with unlimited tokens. 

We haven't decided yet what future content will look like, maybe new rooms with more variety of games, maybe DLC packs of themed games.

Stay tuned and thank you for your continued support. Seriously, I read all the comments here and on reddit and it's really rewarding to see people enjoying what we've created.ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: Quick Match and Bowling Update
notes.content:
Pretty dull but necessary update this time.

We've added a quick match option. This will match you with a public game in your geographic region if one exists. If not then you'll host a public match and someone else might join. [strike]You'll have to back out manually if nothing happens due to ports not being forwarded for the moment. [/strike] The game will time out after 20 seconds if no connection is made. (Forward port 7777 on your routers)

We've also added a private host option for friends only.

On the bowling side we've made it so that the ball doesn't get knocked out of your hand so easily and the unwaxed portion of the alley has been made a bit less frictiony and the ball comes out of the ball return chute instead of appearing out of mid air.

We've also made it so that the toggle grip is disabled if you're already holding something to prevent accidental gripping.

[strike]Also we've recently discovered a network buffer issue which was preventing objects from syncing which we've temporarily fixed by setting everything to all costs messaging which isn't great for performance. We'll switch it back once we find out what's going on.[/strike] 

Should be working now.
